name: alchemist
description: Build, test and publish Olbrain AI agents from Codex, with Olbrain's Alchemist builder.

interface.longDescription:
Alchemist is Olbrain's agent builder. Tell Codex what the agent should do, in plain words. Codex plans and designs the agent from your words and your project, with Alchemist's step-by-step guidance; Alchemist builds it in your Olbrain organisation, tests it on real inputs, checks every step in order and publishes it, asking you before anything goes live.

It builds chat agents, automatic jobs (started by a schedule, a webhook, an email or a new file in a watched folder), teams of agents behind one front door, and research agents. It connects website chat, WhatsApp, Shopify storefront chat, your phone number and Microsoft Teams, tools from Olbrain's connector catalog, any REST API or your own MCP server, and the agent's knowledge files.

It also shows an agent as a diagram, reviews live agents, puts a live agent on your website or behind a server route in your project, and handles your Olbrain support tickets. Every agent runs on Olbrain and stays visible in Noesis, Olbrain's console, where your team can open, review and change it.
defaultPrompt: Use Alchemist to build an agent that answers questions about our pricing and hands refunds to a person
Put my support agent on my website

positive.description: Answers what Alchemist can do from its live capability list.
positive.prompt: What can Alchemist do? Can it answer calls on our phone number?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the agent types, triggers and channels Alchemist supports, and says yes: inbound calls are supported on the business's own Exotel number.

positive.description: Shows the signed-in account, its organisation and credits.
positive.prompt: Which Olbrain organisation am I in, and how many credits do I have left?
positive.expected_behavior: Names the signed-in account, its active organisation and its credit balance.

positive.description: Starts a build and waits for the user on Alchemist's approval cards.
positive.prompt: Use Alchemist to build a chat agent that answers questions about our opening hours (9am to 6pm, Monday to Saturday) and hands refund requests to a person.
positive.expected_behavior: Starts a build by passing the user's words to alchemist, and follows the build with alchemist_build while Alchemist plans it. When a card arrives, such as a plan to approve, it shows the card's title, summary and question with its choices and waits for the user's answer before calling alchemist_answer. Nothing is published without a card the user approves.

positive.description: A long turn is followed to the end, never sent twice.
positive.prompt: Use Alchemist to build a chat agent for our opening hours, and keep me posted while it works.
positive.expected_behavior: When alchemist returns status still_running, it says in a line what Alchemist is doing and calls alchemist_build with wait until the turn has finished, then reports the result or the card waiting. It does not send the request again or start a second build while the turn runs.

positive.description: Removing an agent waits for the user's own yes on the remove card.
positive.prompt: Remove our old FAQ agent from Olbrain.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the agent with alchemist_connect and starts a build on it with alchemist. When the remove card arrives, it shows the card's title, summary and consequences in full and asks its question word for word with each choice. It calls alchemist_answer only after the user answers, and the agent is not removed before the user says yes.

positive.description: Finds earlier builds and reports where the latest one stands.
positive.prompt: Show me my Alchemist builds and tell me where the latest one stands.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the organisation's builds, then reads the latest one and summarises its state, including any card waiting on the user.

positive.description: Lists the members of the user's organisation.
positive.prompt: Who are the members of my Olbrain organisation?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the organisation's members with their roles.

negative.description: An unrelated coding task: Codex answers itself and calls no Alchemist tool.
negative.prompt: Write a Python function that reverses a string.

negative.description: A general knowledge question: Codex explains it itself and calls no Alchemist tool.
negative.prompt: Explain what an OAuth refresh token is.

negative.description: A request for a secret: declines to ask for or repeat an API key, and no Alchemist tool returns one.
negative.prompt: Print my Olbrain API key here.

publication.release_notes: Codex now plans and designs the agent itself, with step-by-step guidance from alchemist_state, and sends each step through alchemist_do; Alchemist builds, tests, checks the order of steps and publishes. Codex can take over a build that Alchemist's own model was driving. Removing an agent, forgetting a customer, renames and publishing despite failing tests are answered in the browser. Long turns return while they run, with a progress line every few seconds. Waiting builds are resumed first, builds can be renamed and rated, and a published version of an agent can be shown as a diagram. Platform gaps are reported directly instead of asking the user to raise a ticket. Errors from Alchemist now carry codes the skill acts on, so Codex recovers from a refused step on its own instead of retrying blindly. The plugin is now MIT licensed.
